national_raw_news.content: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today expressed grief over the loss of lives and devastation caused by the flash floods in Nepal. In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He also prayed for the safe and swift rescue of all those who are missing. Mr Radhakrishnan said that the thoughts of the people of India are with the people of Nepal during this difficult hour. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time. He said, India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. The Prime Minister said, our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for assistance and information regarding Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Nepal today. The Embassy said that people requiring assistance can contact the embassy on helpline +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500. The Embassy said, it has remained engaged with the relevant authorities of Government of Nepal for early rescue and relief for Indian nationals affected by the flash floods. It said, rescue and relief efforts continue to be strengthened in coordination with the Government of Nepal. According to the official sources, India is preparing to send relief material as soon as possible to Nepal. The Tamil Nadu Government has announced a help desk for tourists from Tamil Nadu who have gone to visit Nepal. The Government has appealed to get in touch with the help desk and the State Department for Overseas Affairs. It said that help can also be sought from the Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi. Helplines numbers are 1800 309 3793 and 918069009900. Tamil Nadu House Delhi Help Desk number are 9289516712 and 9180 6900 9901.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 38 Nepal flash floods leave 384 tourists missing, including 105 Indians
national_raw_news.content: More than 100 Indians are among 384 tourists reported missing in Nepal after flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River hit the Rasuwa region near the Tibet border this morning. According to the Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) the 384 missing tourists include 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali citizens. It said, the foreign nationals are from several countries, including 105 from India, and others from the United Kingdom, Australia, the United States, Malaysia, South Africa and the Netherlands. However, the NTB clarified that the figures are preliminary and are currently being verified and cross-checked with travel agencies, local authorities and other concerned agencies. According to local media reports, seven people have died following the massive flash flood. Preliminary information suggests that the flash flood was caused by an earthquake triggering an avalanche with melted snow pouring into the Bhote Koshi river. The flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River caused a major disruption in the Rasuwa region, triggering concerns over the safety of tourists and other people present in the affected areas. Authorities and rescue agencies are continuing efforts to assess the situation and establish the whereabouts of those reported missing. The Nepal Tourism Board has also issued emergency contact numbers for tourists and their families seeking information or assistance. The emergency contacts include the toll-free number 1234, the hotline 1144 and the Tourist Police number 9851289445. The tourism board urged tourists in the affected areas to remain calm, stay informed through official channels and follow all safety instructions issued by the authorities. In view of the situation, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah has consulted with federal parliamentarians from the affected areas, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan. The discussion focused on the damage caused by the flash flood, the condition of coastal settlements, and rescue and relief efforts. Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah had convened a meeting of the National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management to review the situation in the flood-affected areas and the progress of rescue, search and relief efforts. Search and rescue operations are underway, and further details are awaited.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 10 Bihar steps up flood preparedness amid possibility of rise in Gandak River
national_raw_news.content: Bihar has stepped up flood preparedness following flash floods in Nepal and the possibility of a sudden rise in the water level of the Gandak River. Six districts of the state – West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali – have been placed under heightened vigilance along the Gandak river system. Besides, District Magistrates of Sitamarhi, Sheohar and other districts have also been directed to keep a close and continuous watch on the situation. People living in low-lying areas of Bagaha in West Champaran and Vaishali district have been urged to move to safer places at the earliest. In view of the possibility of increased water flow in the Gandak River, an NDRF team has been deployed in Gopalganj and Bettiah, while another team has been kept on standby in Muzaffarpur. Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary said that a high-level team has been constituted to closely monitor the situation. In view of the situation, a high-level review meeting was held today in Patna under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit. District Magistrates and senior police officials of the concerned districts have been directed to maintain round-the-clock surveillance and keep rescue and relief arrangements on standby. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also spoke to Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the phone in view of the flood threat in Bihar due to torrential rain and glacier burst in Nepal. Home Minister assured the state government of providing all possible assistance to deal with the emerging situation. Mr Shah added that National Disaster Response Force is being mobilised to deal with the situation.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 150 FM Nirmala Sitharaman says India’s transformation is structural, driven by rapid urbanisati...
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India stands as the fastest-growing major economy in the world and offers a unique combination of scale, sustained growth, a young population, expanding consumption and rapidly deepening capital markets. Addressing prominent members of the Indian business community in Toronto today, Sitharaman said India’s transformation is structural, driven by rapid urbanisation, a growing middle class and world-class digital infrastructure. She noted that these developments are creating new opportunities across virtually every sector of the economy. The Finance Minister also highlighted the role of India’s digital ecosystem in transforming access to financial and commercial services. She underlined significant opportunities for collaboration with Canadian banks, fintech companies and regulators, not only in payments but also in shaping the next generation of digital financial infrastructure. Highlighting the growing India-Canada economic partnership, Sitharaman said the Indian diaspora in Canada serves as a strategic bridge between the two countries. She said India-Canada bilateral ties have undergone a remarkable transformation in recent times, supported by shared democratic and pluralistic values, expanding economic engagement, high-level interactions and strong people-to-people ties. Referring to the agreement reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Mark Carney on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in June 2025 to reset bilateral ties, Sitharaman said the two countries have reaffirmed their commitment to building a future-focused strategic partnership. Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman arrived in Toronto yesterday for a four-day official visit to Canada, focused on strengthening bilateral trade, investment linkages and financial cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi Government hands over approval letters to 4,000 women under Lakshmi Yojana 31 mins ago 14
national_raw_news.content: The Delhi Government today handed over the approval letters to the 4 thousand eligible women beneficiaries under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana out of which 2 thousand 500 letter given at the formal ceremony. Under the scheme, eligible women will receive financial assistance of 2 thousand 500 rupees every month. Speaking on the occasion, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu said that this initiative is a significant step towards women’s welfare, empowerment, and dignity. He also highlighted the importance of empowering women and ensuring their rightful place in the social and economic development of the nation. Our correspondent reports that the monthly assistance will strengthen financial security, everyday choice and self-reliance. The Delhi Government has finalised the manner in which the assistance can be disbursed. Eligible women will receive one thousand rupees every month through a digital wallet and one thousand 500 rupees will be deposited as a fixed deposit, with interest to be borne by the government. Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that this initiative is a significant step towards women’s welfare, empowerment and dignity. She added that this financial assistance can help women meet important needs, including children’s care and education, household requirements or support for their livelihood and business activities. Around nine lakh thirteen thousand women registered for the scheme and over six lakh 52 thousand applications were submitted. The Delhi government said that the financial assistance will be credited directly to women beneficiary’s bank accounts from 1st of next month. A financial outlay of five thousand one hundred 10 crore rupees has been made for the scheme in the 2026-27 Delhi Budget. The response to the scheme reflects the confidence Delhi’s women have placed in this initiative and strengthens the Government’s resolve to widen opportunity and empowerment across the capital.
